title: Former Penn State 1,000-Yard WR Labeled as NFL's Most Overpaid WR
description: Penn State has sent plenty of good players to the NFL over the years, with Saquon Barkley being one of the best. He earned a huge payday from the Philadelphia Eagles and is well worth his huge extension.
fullText:
Penn State has sent plenty of good players to the NFL over the years, with Saquon Barkley being one of the best. He earned a huge payday from the Philadelphia Eagles and is well worth his huge extension.

But not all of the former Nittany Lions players in the NFL are worth as much as they are getting paid right now. Some are earning more than they maybe should, considering their talents.

In Garrett Podell of CBS Sports' opinion, one former Penn State wide receiver, who had over 1,000 yards in one season with the Nittany Lions, is the most overpaid WR in the NFL. That WR is Tampa Bay Buccaneers veteran Chris Godwin.

"Chris Godwin's three-year, $66 million extension is aging like spoiled milk," Podell writes. "He has missed a combined 18 games over the last two seasons, eight of which came in 2025, when he registered career lows in catches (33) and receiving yards (360) while producing the second-fewest receiving touchdowns of his career (two)."

Godwin is a 30-year-old wide receiver who was drafted in the third round, at 84th overall, by the Buccaneers back in 2017.

He's since won a Super Bowl, catching passes from Tom Brady, and was named a Pro Bowler back in 2019 when he had 1,333 receiving yards.

In his NFL career, Godwin has 612 receptions on 867 targets for 7,626 yards and 41 touchdowns. He's also one first-down shy of 400 for his NFL career.

Godwin is one of the best WRs to come out of Penn State in school history, but now, at 30 years old entering his 10th season in the league, he's considered the most overpaid WR in the league.

Spending $22 million per-year on Godwin is a bit too much, considering he just had back-to-back seasons playing under 10 games and recording under 600 receiving yards.

During his time at Penn State, only his freshman season, when he caught 26 passes for 338 yards and two TDs, was worse. He had 1,101 yards and five TDS in 2015, and 982 yards and 11 TDs in 2016.

While Godwin could bounce back in 2026 for the Buccaneers, the former Penn State star WR is currently overpaid and is arguably the most overpaid WR in the NFL.

But even if he doesn't do a whole lot more for the rest of his NFL career, it's still been a massive success for the Nittany Lions WR in the NFL, as he's been arguably the best WR Penn State has ever sent to the league.

title: NFL predictions: Previewing all 16 AFC teams & predicting every record in 2026
description: Division winners, win totals, playoff teams, and more!
fullText:
The 2026 NFL season is almost here, and the AFC looks loaded from top to bottom. Every division has at least one legitimate contender, while several teams could make the jump from afterthought to playoff team. Here is my division-by-division breakdown and prediction for all 16 AFC teams.

MORE: 5 most improved NFL offenses entering 2026-2027 season

Dec 21, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) warms up prior to a game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images

The Bills remain the safest bet in this division. Josh Allen is still the centerpiece, but the biggest change comes with Joe Brady taking over as head coach and Jim Leonhard running the defense. Buffalo also added DJ Moore to a receiving corps that desperately needed another difference-maker. The Bills won 12 games last season, and I expect them to remain near the top of the AFC. Prediction: 11-6, AFC East champions.

It's difficult to bet against the reigning AFC champions after what they accomplished last season. Drake Maye has another year of experience, and New England added A.J. Brown to an offense that already averaged 28.8 points per game in 2025. The Patriots will have enormous expectations, but I expect them to remain a serious contender. Prediction: 11-6, playoff team.

The Jets are better than the Dolphins, but that's not saying much. Geno Smith returns after leading the NFL in interceptions last season, while New York has completely reshaped its roster and enters 2026 with three first-round picks. There is enough talent here to surprise people, but the quarterback play has to improve dramatically. Prediction: 6-11.

Miami feels like a rebuilding team after moving on from Tua Tagovailoa and Tyreek Hill. Malik Willis now has an enormous opportunity, but expecting everything to click immediately is asking a lot. The Dolphins could be competitive in stretches, but this looks like the toughest roster in the division. Prediction: 5-12.

Dec 7, 2025; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) warms up before the game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Casey-Imagn Images

The Ravens are my pick to bounce back after an ugly 8-9 season. John Harbaugh is gone, and Jesse Minter takes over, while Lamar Jackson gets a new offensive coordinator in Declan Doyle. Baltimore also added Trey Hendrickson and could get Nnamdi Madubuike back, potentially transforming a defense that struggled badly last year. Prediction: 11-6, AFC North champions.

Joe Burrow's health remains the biggest variable, but Cincinnati finally appears serious about fixing its defense. The Bengals added Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger before acquiring Dexter Lawrence. If Burrow stays healthy, this could be a dangerous team. Prediction: 10-7, playoff team.

The Steelers are fascinating because Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers could either make this look like a brilliant move or a desperate one. Pittsburgh also added Michael Pittman Jr., giving Rodgers another legitimate target. The defense has to improve, though, after ranking 26th in total defense last season. Prediction: 9-8.

The Browns are still rebuilding. Todd Monken takes over as head coach, the quarterback situation remains unsettled, and Cleveland traded Myles Garrett after his record-setting 2025 season. Jared Verse gives the defense a new centerpiece, but I don't expect the Browns to contend yet. Prediction: 5-12.

Division winner: Baltimore Ravens

MORE: 4 NFL players with most pressure entering 2026-2027 season

Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) throws during the first half of an AFC Wild Card Round game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium. Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images

The Texans are one of the most difficult teams to project. They went 12-5 last season and have an outstanding defense, but C.J. Stroud needs to rediscover his rookie form. Houston also completely revamped its offensive line and added David Montgomery to improve the running game. If the line finally stabilizes, the Texans could be a Super Bowl contender. Prediction: 11-6, AFC South champions.

Jacksonville won 13 games last season and remains one of the AFC's most intriguing teams. Travis Etienne is gone, leaving Bhayshul Tuten and others to replace his production, while Travis Hunter's two-way role will be fascinating to watch. If Brian Thomas Jr. takes a step forward, and Parker Washington continues his ascent, this offense could be dangerous. Prediction: 10-7, playoff team.

The Colts' entire season may depend on Daniel Jones staying healthy. Indianapolis saw its offense fall apart when Jones was injured last year, and the team is also dealing with major health questions involving Jonathan Taylor and DeForest Buckner. There's talent here, but too much uncertainty for me to trust them as a playoff team. Prediction: 8-9.

Everything revolves around Cam Ward. Tennessee brought in Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll to help develop its young quarterback and added veteran receiver Wan'Dale Robinson along with first-round pick Carnell Tate. I expect improvement, but the Titans are still a year away from seriously competing. Prediction: 6-11.

Division winner: Houston Texans

Jan 17, 2026; Denver, CO, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) calls an audible during the first quarter of an AFC Divisional Round playoff game against the Buffalo Bills at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Denver is my pick to win the AFC West. The Broncos went 14-3 last season, largely kept their roster intact, and added Jaylen Waddle to give Bo Nix another elite weapon. The biggest question is Nix's health after his ankle injury, but if he's healthy, Denver has the most complete roster in the division. Prediction: 12-5, AFC West champions.

The Chiefs are coming off a stunning 6-11 season, so there's nowhere to go but up. Patrick Mahomes remains the ultimate reason for optimism, but Kansas City has more questions than we've seen in years. I expect a bounce-back season, just not another dominant run through the division. Prediction: 10-7, playoff team.

The Chargers should once again be competitive with Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh, but their offensive line health remains a concern. The addition of tight end David Njoku gives Herbert more options, and the defense should keep them in games. Still, I don't see them winning this division. Prediction: 9-8.

The Raiders may be the AFC's most intriguing long-term project. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is behind veteran Kirk Cousins for now, while Las Vegas also made significant offensive-line upgrades. If Cousins struggles, the pressure to unleash Mendoza will become enormous. Prediction: 6-11.

Division winner: Denver Broncos

Aug 15, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) on field against the Los Angeles Rams during the first half of the pre season game at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

My AFC playoff field would be Buffalo, Baltimore, Houston and Denver as division winners, with New England and Cincinnati, and Kansas City earning wild-card spots.

The AFC should be extremely competitive, but I see Denver, Baltimore and Houston as the three teams best positioned to challenge Buffalo and New England for the conference crown. There are plenty of variables that could change the picture once the regular season begins, but on paper, the AFC looks like it could be an absolute battle from Week 1 through the playoffs.

title: ‘No Pity From Me,’ ‘Should’ve Booed Louder’ — Deshaun Watson Gets on NFL Fans’ Nerves After Divisive Remarks on Getting Booed at Home
description: Deshaun Watson’s comments after the Cleveland Browns’ 31-7 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills have added another layer to the team’s ongoing quarterback drama. Watson was met with loud boos when he entered the game in the second half after Shedeur Sanders started the contest.
fullText:
Deshaun Watson's comments after the Cleveland Browns' 31-7 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills have added another layer to the team's ongoing quarterback drama.

Watson was met with loud boos when he entered the game in the second half after Shedeur Sanders started the contest. Afterward, Watson called the reaction "disrespectful" and "personal," prompting an immediate response from NFL fans.

The boos rang out as soon as Watson's name was announced at the beginning of the second half. Speaking after the game, Watson said he believes the reaction went beyond his on-field performance.

"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said after Saturday's preseason action. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think that's a disrespectful thing."

Watson also referenced his previous injury (from back in 2024) in Cleveland, adding, "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fanbase, they cheered when I got hurt."

His comments quickly spread across social media, with fans largely pushing back against the quarterback's perspective.

Pranav Sriraman summed up his reaction bluntly: "Should've booed louder."

NFL analyst Max Loeb also suggested Watson's comments showed just how strained the relationship has become. "If you didn't think things were already too far gone in Cleveland with Deshaun Watson… Watch this clip."

Joey Knish questioned why Watson remains with the Browns at all: "Why the [expletive] is this guy even on the team? The Browns want to lose and draft a QB. The fanbase HATES Watson. There's a 0% chance anybody trades for him. Just send his [expletive] home."

Kev focused on what he viewed as Watson portraying himself as the victim. "This guy playing the victim card is wild for 100 reasons." A co-host at Fox Sports Radio even suggested the Browns should consider moving on immediately: "Send him to the NY Jets and get this [expletive] over with before it gets ugly."

Analyst Jared Monroe offered one of the harshest assessments of Watson's situation in Cleveland: "No pity from me. You can either be a bad person or bad at your job. You can't be both. Deshaun's wasted guaranteed bag set the Browns back more than a decade."

NFL writerBrian Drake was similarly critical, arguing that Watson's relationship with the fanbase may be beyond repair: "Browns owe Deshaun Watson $46M guaranteed. But it's over. The fans will never accept him after his scumbag actions. Make him inactive every week, then move on. He'll likely never play another down in the NFL."

The reaction comes as Cleveland continues to evaluate Watson and second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders.

Sanders started the second preseason matchup and immediately provided a spark. He completed his first eight passes and capped Cleveland's opening drive with an 8-yard touchdown pass to Luke Floriea.

Watson struggled after taking over in the second half. He completed 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and threw an interception as Cleveland's offense failed to find any rhythm.

With head coach Todd Monken yet to announce a Week 1 starter ahead of the Browns' opener against Jacksonville, the game against Buffalo only added to the debate.

For Cleveland, the decision now involves more than simply comparing two quarterbacks. Sanders has energized the fanbase, while Watson is facing increasing frustration from supporters who have already made their feelings clear.

The Browns will ultimately have to decide whether Watson's experience and contract situation outweigh Sanders' momentum and growing support in Cleveland.

title: Rams backups highlight the NFL's flawed beauty in 34-0 win over Saints
description: One play. A lifetime of waiting. Alex Cook's 100-yard interception return for a touchdown was a prayer whispered into existence. But in the cruel mathematics of NFL, one moment of glory might not be enough. Read the story of the Rams' 34-0 shutout and the men fighting for one more tomorrow.
fullText:
INGLEWOOD, Calif.––Thousands of football fans traveled through an asphalt skillet and sun-baking rays to sit in SoFi Stadium air thick with the smell of polyethylene pellets and concession food, littering empty seats and staring down at a field full of men fighting for their lives.

Peter Pan lost his shadow in Wendy Darling's nursery. Peter Pan never played football. Peter Pan never had to stare down the barrel of an NFL roster cut or feel the August sun bake his last hope into the turf.

Not the marquee names. The other ones.

The marquee names are set. The stars sleep in their beds while the backups, the special teamers and the practice-squad hopefuls run themselves into the ground for 60 minutes of tape that might buy them 60 more days in a uniform.

The ones who know the difference between making the 53-man roster and making a phone call home that changes everything.

For one afternoon in Inglewood, the Rams' backups played like they had nothing to lose and everything to prove.

The New Orleans Saints never stood a chance in the 34-0 drubbing.

For most of these men, the dream of regular-season action is not dying; it is already dead.

But on this Saturday in Inglewood, the dead refused to lie down.

Cam Lampkin has been the shadow of every receiver he covered.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cam Lampkin (21) daps up with teammates during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

At 5-foot-11 he is not the biggest name in the Rams secondary.

He is neither Trent McDuffie nor Jaylen Watson.

Lampkin is a name many overlook when they check the depth chart. But on Saturday, he made Zach Wilson feel like Captain Hook in the first half––searching, swiping, finding nothing but empty air and regret.

Wilson dropped back––looked left, looked right. Wilson found only the sticky fingers of coverage. The pass rush and coverage have a symbiotic relationship; one hand washes the other. Even without Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, McDuffie or Watson playing, the New Orleans Saints stood no chance against Los Angeles' coverage unit.

Wilson completed just 6 of 12 passes for 55 yards in the first half and an abysmal 28.1 quarterback rating. The kind of number that gets a man cut before the team plane lands.

Lampkin played with coverage so sticky that Super Glue would envy. Every receiver he faced found a shadow that moved with them, anticipated their breaks and swallowed their hope.

"He did a great job," Sean McVay said. "You know, I thought we were in positions to understand a lot of the coverages."

Al'Zillion Hamilton jumped a hook route early in the second quarter. Wilson threw it right to him. It was the kind of play that separates guys who stick around from guys who don't. It was not merely an interception; it was an invitation accepted.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett IV (13) hands the ball off during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Then Stetson Bennett took over.

He played like a man possessed, completing 19 of 31 passes for 181 yards and rushing for two touchdowns.

He scrambled when the pocket collapsed. He scrambled to make plays. He scrambled for his football life.

It started in the first quarter. Fourth and 1.

Bennett feathered a pass over double coverage to Tyler Scott, who laid out like a man diving for loose change on a sidewalk. Scott had an earlier ball bounce off his hand on a would-be touchdown, but this time, he held on.

"The flat guy got ran into," Bennett said. "I was just thinking put it in a safe spot so T Scott (Tyler Scott) can go get it."

The drive stalled in the red zone, and Harrison Mevis netted a 26-yard field goal to give the Rams backups a leap forward and a 3-0 score.

Bennet later scored on a 1-yard scramble after the refs deliberated and later ruled it a touchdown. Mevis nailed the PAT to extend the lead 10-0.

In the second quarter, with the Saints in man-to-man coverage and no one on the defense accounting for him, Bennett scrambled to the right when Saints edge rusher Garrett Nelson didn't keep containment.

Bennett looked like a gamer and orchestrated scoring drives throughout the game.

"It feels more comfortable out there than in years prior," Bennett said.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

Los Angeles Rams defensive back Alex Cook (39) runs to the end zone for a touchdown during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Alex Cook has not played in the NFL since 2023. He came from the UFL. He dreamed of being back. He dreamed of one more pick-six.

In the third quarter, Spencer Rattler drove the Saints down the field. The goal line loomed. The Rams' defense bent. Rattler threw to Treyton Welch on a hitch route.

Drove on the ball. Undercut the route. Caught it in stride.

Then he ran 100 yards for a pick-six that stretched the Rams' lead to 27-0 and sucked whatever life remained out of the Saints' sideline.

A lifetime of waiting collapsed into 15 seconds of glory.

"I was dreaming like, man, if I could just get one more pick six back in the NFL, that would make my whole life," Cook said. "Thank God I was able to get one today."

He finished with one tackle on defense and one on special teams. One hundred yards on one play. One tackle on every other play. The math of the NFL is cruel; the NFL's poetry––astonishing.

Cook's journey to this moment was anything but linear. He came from the UFL. He has fought, scratched and clawed his way back onto an NFL sideline. The Rams gave him a chance; he is not wasting it.

"We were in a typical cover four," Cook explained. "I knew that spot route was going to come sit right at the end zone and I was just waiting for the QB to throw."

When the throw came, Cook jumped it. He had inside leverage. He had position. He had the instincts of a player who has been doing this since he was a kid.

"I need some more oxygen," Cook joked. "I was beyond tired. But seriously, you just got to reset your mind. It's the next play mentality."

The sideline celebration told a different story. Teammates mobbed him. They recognized what the moment meant. For him. For his carrer. For his life.

"That was so cool," Cook said. "That just a testament of this team and the culture Sean McVay has built."

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

The New Orleans Saints fumble the ball near the end zone during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Then Wesley Bailey, who lived in the backfield, forced a fumble. in the third quarter.

The Saints had driven deep into Rams territory. A touchdown would cut into the lead. Bailey punched the ball free from Ty Chandler, and Payton Zdroik recovered at the 2-yard line.

A red-zone turnover. A momentum killer. A difference.

Bailey finished with five tackles, a sack, three pressures, a tackle for loss, a forced fumble and four QB hits––a performance so complete that McVay couldn't stop talking about it.

"You felt his presence all day," McVay said. "There's certain guys you just kind of feel on defense where you just know they're making their presence felt."

"Being able to get a red zone turnover is great," Bailey said. "For him to come out with nothing is definitely great."

But the final score is not the story.

The story is what happens next week when the coaching staff gathers in a room and decides who gets to keep chasing their dream and who gets a handshake, a thank-you, and a phone number for their agent.

Sean McVay stood at the podium. His voice carried the weight of a man who has been on both sides of these cuts.

"I thought it was a really just good team effort," McVay said. "Awesome to see so many guys making plays."

He praised Bennett's command. He praised Bailey's presence. He praised the secondary.

"Repetition is the mother of learning," McVay said.

But repetition is also the father of heartbreak.

These players have repeated the drills. They have repeated the routes. They have repeated the dream. Soon, they will wait.

Edwin So - The Sporting Tribune

New Orleans Saints quarterback Spencer Rattler (2) makes a pass during an NFL preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and Los Angeles Rams on Saturday, August 22, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

The Los Angeles Rams' second preseason game was much more stress-free than the first.

Neither team played its starters. But the Rams' backups were clearly much better than New Orleans'. It is a compliment to the depth the Rams have developed across the roster.

But depth is a double-edged sword.

Depth means the team is strong. Depth also means the bubble is crowded.

For Alex Cook, 100 yards might not be enough to make the 53-man roster.

The numbers are cruel that way.

But he gave himself something that can't be taken away––an opportunity.

His film will be reviewed. And if the Rams don't keep him, another team might.

For Bailey, the undrafted free agent out of Louisville, it will be hard to leave him off the 53-man roster. He brings speed, athleticism, length on the edge and was dominant against the Saints.

But August dominance does not guarantee September employment.

For Lampkin, who has been cut twice and signed twice, this game was another chapter in a story written in invisible ink.

For Hamilton, the interception was a line on a resume that might get him a job in another city.

For most of these players, their dreams of regular-season action in the NFL are quickly coming to a close.

Cuts are looming, and they are near.

Phone calls will be made, tears shed, hearts broken — football lives will die.

But for one afternoon, they were all Rams.

They all fought; some made plays.

"I thought it was a really just good team effort," McVay said.

He was right. But it was also so much more. A reminder that every snap matters. Every catch, every tackle, every interception, every forced fumble matters.

Because for the men who make the most of them, those moments might be the difference between a locker and a phone call home.

A difference between a dream and a memory.

Peter Pan never had to fight for a roster spot. Peter Pan never had to run 100 yards to prove he belonged. Peter Pan's got his shadow back.

These men are still searching for theirs.

title: What Happened to Josh Jacobs? Latest on the Packers RB’s Legal Situation and Whether He’ll Be Suspended by NFL
description: Josh Jacobs entered Green Bay Packers training camp with two separate questions hanging over his 2026 season. One involves a groin injury.
fullText:
Josh Jacobs entered Green Bay Packers training camp with two separate questions hanging over his 2026 season. One involves a groin injury. The more serious one involves an unresolvedlegal matter and the possibility of NFL discipline.

No suspension has been announced yet, but Jacobs remains under review by the league after his May arrest, while the Brown County District Attorney's Office has not filed formal criminal charges.

Police responded to a disturbance complaint involving Jacobs on May 23 in Hobart, Wis. He wasarrested and booked into Brown County Jail on suspicion of battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, and intimidation of a victim.

Jacobs' attorneys said he "vehemently denies the allegations." The running back wasreleased from custody on May 27 after prosecutors said they were not prepared to make a formal charging decision and had requested additional investigation.

The case has remained unresolved. The Brown County District Attorney's Office said in late July that the investigation was "still open" and an update would be provided once a resolution was reached. Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst also described it as anongoing legal situation, with Green Bay and the NFL waiting for the process to play out.

That distinction is important. Jacobs was arrested, but as of Aug. 21, no formal criminal charges have been filed against him.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

A suspension remains possible, but it is not confirmed.

ESPN's Adam Schefterreported Aug. 11 that Jacobs' situation is "still under review" and remains a "pending situation" with the NFL. Schefter said discipline is still a potential option as the league works through several unresolved player cases before the regular season.

The NFL'sconduct policy allows discipline independent of the outcome of a criminal case. Its baseline punishment for a violation involving assault, battery, or domestic violence is six games without pay, although mitigating or aggravating circumstances can change the length.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Green Bay therefore cannot assume Jacobs will be available when it opens the season Sept. 13 at the Minnesota Vikings, according to theofficial schedule. The league has not announced a decision or timetable.

His potential absence would be substantial. Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 15 games last season while adding 282 receiving yards and another score. He posted a 76.5 PFN RB Impact score last season, ranking 16th among qualifying running backs.

For now, Jacobs remains eligible to participate when healthy. He is also working back from the separate groin injury that has limited him during camp.

The legal process and the NFL review are moving on different tracks. Until either produces a resolution, Green Bay's Week 1 backfield comes with an unusually large asterisk.

Last season, both the Chiefs and the Texans were underwhelming offensively. Kansas City finished at number 13 on PFN's Offense Impact Metric, while Houston dropped all the way to number 21.

For both teams, some of those numbers could be attributed to injuries. For the Chiefs, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL near the end of the season, while both Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy missed significant chunks of the year.

The Texans, on the other hand, had C.J. Stroud and Nico Collins miss some games, while Tank Dell was out for the entire season. Neither team, though, has made any major upgrades to their passing game, as they expect improved health to carry them forward.

But while the Texans have the star power, at least on paper, a torn ACL has sidelined Jayden Higgins for the entire season. Meanwhile, the Chiefs' receiving corps looks far from a unit that is poised to compete for a playoff spot.

As a result, Ryan Wilson of CBS Sports, who was making a case for Tyreek Hill to find his next team in the NFL, had those two squads near the top of the list. He believed that the eight-time Pro Bowler could be a needle mover for some team later down the line.

title: Patriots scouting report: Elijah Ponder is an explosive athlete on the edge
description: Previewing the Patriots edge defender heading into his second NFL season.
fullText:
The New England Patriots entered the 2025 NFL Draft facing significant questions at multiple positions, including the defensive edge. However, their investments were relatively minimal. In fact, their best contributions from a rookie edge last season came not from a draft pick but an undrafted free agent.

Heading into his second season in the league, Elijah Ponder now is looking ready to play an even more prominent role.

Position: Defensive edge/Outside linebacker

Opening day age: 24 (8/24/2002)

Measurements: 6'2 7/8", 261 lbs, 10 1/8" hand size, 33 1/8" arm length, 80" wingspan, 4.63s 40-yard dash, 6.99s 3-cone drill, 4.28s short shuttle, 41" vertical jump, 11'0" broad jump, 22 bench press reps, 9.87 Relative Athletic Score

NFL:New England Patriots (2025-) | College: Cal Poly (2020-24)

A multi-sport athlete at Bishop Amat High School in La Puente, CA, Ponder received some FCS interest as a two-star outside linebacker recruit. Ultimately, however, he decided to head for the FBS and joined Cal Poly. In five seasons with the Mustangs, he saw action in 47 games with 42 starts. He also registered 26.5 sacks and 43.5 tackles for loss, and was named All-Big Sky in all four of his non-redshirt campaigns (first team 2023, 2024; honorable mention 2021, 2022).

Despite his college success, Ponder did not hear his name called in the 2025 NFL Draft. He joined the Patriots as an undrafted free agent afterwards and appeared in 19 games as a rookie with four sacks and three fumble recoveries.

Strengths: Checking in at 6-foot-3 and 261 pounds, Ponder offers good size on the defensive edge. He combines it with an intriguing athletic skillset; his explosivity, agility and speed are rare, and he looks the part on the field as well. He is quick to attack the pocket and has the burst to challenge blockers' leverage and balance early into a rep, plays with active hands, and can properly bend the corner around the edge. He also has good spatial awareness, which in turn allows him to locate the football effectively even in traffic, and the range to be a factor in pursuit.

Weaknesses: Ponder moves as well as any outside linebacker in football, but he fails to consistently look the part on the field. His game speed and timed speed do not always align, in parts because he is still a developing player from a technical and processing perspective. He also lacks ideal length and is not the most powerful player at the point of attack. He furthermore is a pass-first player whose contributions against the run have been limited so far. When he has been asked to play the run, he has failed to consistently set the edge and contain runs to the inside.

Stats: 19 games (0 starts) | 314 defensive snaps (24.5%), 287 special teams snaps (52.4%) | 17 tackles, 1 missed tackle (5.6%), 4 TFLs, 2 FRs | 24 QB pressures (4 sacks, 3 hits, 17 hurries) | 11 special teams tackles, 3 missed tackles (21.4%), 1 FR | 3 penalties (incl. 0 declined/offsetting)

Season recap: Despite his small-school status, Ponder was invited to both the Hula Bowl and the East-West Shrine Bowl heading toward the draft. As noted above, however, he was not selected in any of the seven rounds and had to navigate the free agency waters before finding a home in the NFL. The journey, however, was a rather short one: he joined the Patriots as one of their first-wave UDFA signings.

While that meant he started out buried on the depth chart, Ponder steadily climbed his way up the ranks. Strong showings in training camp and preseason ultimately allowed him to join wide receiver Efton Chism as the only two undrafted rookies to make New England's initial 53-man roster. Even though he lacked pedigree, he remained there throughout the sesaon.

Early on, Ponder was mostly a special teamer. Even as his defensive role evolved, he kept seeing regular action as a four-unit contributor in the kicking game to eventually finish sixth among his teammates in snaps and third in tackles.

On defense, meanwhile, he saw a handful of snaps over the first half of the season. However, with starting edge Harold Landry starting to deal with nagging injury woes, he managed to grow his role: from Week 12 on, when Landry's issues started impacting his availability, Ponder was on the field for roughly 36.8% of snaps. Those snaps came predominately in the passing game, with early-down duties falling on fellow edge Anfernee Jennings.

In that relatively specialized role, Ponder delivered some good performances. In fact, his affinity for finding the football and recovering fumbles — his three FRs were tied for the team lead in 2025 — turned out crucial: he helped set up the only touchdown of the Patriots' AFC Championship win in Denver (and in fact would have scored himself on the play if not for a bad call by the officials).

BALL WAS OUT – GOING THE OTHER WAY‼️

📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/swmdTx0TYV

All in all, Ponder had a very good first season in the NFL. It may not have started as he had hoped by not hearing his name called in the draft, but his effort and playmaking abilities earned him his way onto the Patriots' roster. Once there, he showed that he belonged.

Position: Outside linebacker | Ability: Depth player/Role player | Contract: Signed through 2027 (2028 RFA)

What will be his role? Ponder has worked as an outside linebacker throughout training camp so far, and in fact has been a regular as the starter opposite Dre'Mont Jones. While Harold Landry's eventual return from the physically unable to perform list will shake things up, Ponder currently projects as a rotational third or fourth option at the position as well as a key special teamer.

What is his growth potential? From an athletic perspective, Ponder's ceiling is sky-high. There are, however, questions about how far he can actually still climb and whether he can become more than a depth piece. If he can clean up his own personal operation, there is no reason to believe that he can't be a serviceable third or fourth member in an edge room.

Does he have positional versatility? Defensively, Ponder's versatility is somewhat limited; he is mostly a pass rusher at this point in his development. However, the game's third phase is a different story. On special teams, he played at least 45 snaps on each of the core four units (kickoff return, kickoff coverage, punt return, punt coverage) and there is no reason to believe he can't play a similar role in 2026.

What is his salary cap situation? Arriving via a standard three-year UDFA deal last offseason, Ponder is carrying a $1.01 million cap number into the coming season. That number consists almost entirely of his $1.005 million base salary as well as a $5,000 signing bonus proration. That bonus is the only part of the deal guaranteed, which means that it also is currently his only trace in New England's books under the NFL's Top 51 role.

How safe is his roster spot? Heading into the second preseason game, anything but Ponder making the 53-man roster would be a surprise. He has been the top option to replace Harold Landry in the lineup, after all, and has had some positive moments throughout training camp. Add his special teams role and he should be expected on the active team come the fall.

Summary: Ponder is one of those players who won't be able to make the game-changing plays or demand special attention on a weekly basis. That said, he is still immensely valuable to the operation but defensively and in the kicking game.

What do you think about Elijah Ponder heading into the 2026 season? Will he increase his role? Or will he cede snaps to rookie Gabe Jacas? Please head down to the comment section to share your thoughts with the rest of the community.

title: Former Washington QB gets next NFL shot with New York Giants
description: Former Washington Huskies quarterback Jake Haener signed with the New York Giants on Monday, where he will compete for a backup job.
fullText:
Jake Haener has earned another shot at an NFL roster.

The former Washington quarterback, who was taken in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL draft by the New Orleans Saints after transferring from Montlake to Fresno State, signed with the New York Giants on Monday morning. It's Haener's third team in 2026 after finishing the 2025 regular season on the Saints practice squad, then signing a reserve/futures contract with the Kansas City Chiefs before being waived in May.

The #Giants are signing veteran QB Jake Haener, source says. Haener, who had worked out for the team late last month, lands in East Rutherford after a few workouts with other teams. pic.twitter.com/s0TjX8Iojo

Haener appeared in only 4 games at Washington, all in 2018, completing 9 of his 13 passes for 107 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. He nearly returned to the Huskies in 2022; however, after Washington hired Fresno State coach Kalen DeBoer to replace Jimmy Lake. DeBoer wanted Haener to follow him back to Montlake, but a credits issue and the subsequent re-hire of Jeff Tedford at Fresno State kept Haener with the Bulldogs. DeBoer pivoted to Indiana quarterback Michael Penix Jr., whom he had coached as the Hoosiers' offensive coordinator in 2019.

That decision, of course, worked out for Washington. Penix went on to become a Heisman finalist and led the Huskies to a national championship game appearance in 2023 before being selected No. 8 overall by the Atlanta Falcons in the 2024 NFL draft.

Haener has played in 8 NFL games, starting 1, all for the Saints in 2024. He has completed 18 of 39 career passing attempts for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception. But after Giants third-string quarterback Brandon Allen struggled in the team's first preseason game, Haener has a real opportunity to win that job and join second-year passer Jaxson Dart and veteran backup Jameis Winston in New York's quarterback room.

After transferring to Fresno State, Haener set the program record for career completion percentage at 68.1 percent, finished in the top five of every major passing statistic, earned All-Mountain West honors twice, was named a captain all three years, and was named MVP of the 2023 Senior Bowl. He is one of three Bulldogs to throw for at least 4,000 yards in a season, along with brothers David and Derek Carr.

The Giants travel to Florida to play the Miami Dolphins on Saturday for their second of three preseason games. New York ends their preseason with a crosstown game against the New York Jets on August 28, two days before the 53-man roster deadline.

fullText:

title: See where PFF ranked Zach Allen among NFL’s best interior linemen
description: Broncos star Zach Allen is one of the best IDL's in the NFL. Where should he be ranked?
fullText:
When the Denver Broncos signed Zach Allen to a three-year, $45.75 million deal in March 2023, the team got a great bargain.

Allen was selected in the third round of the 2019 NFL draft by the Arizona Cardinals, and while he was good there, he flew well under the radar. The Broncos knew they were getting a cornerstone piece for their defense. They knew they were getting a perfect fit for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, who coached Allen with the Cards.

In three years, Allen has built on the success he started in Arizona and transformed into one of the league's best interior defensive linemen. He was selected as a first-team All-Pro last season while also making his first Pro Bowl.

However, when Gordon McGuinness of Pro Football Focus ranked the top interior defensive linemen in the league, Allen only came in at No. 10. Broncos fans are going to argue that is too low, and it probably is, but the league is stocked with some tremendous talent at this position.

"Allen's PFF grade has been pulled down some by his struggles against the run, but he's become one of the more reliable interior pass-rushers in football," McGuinness wrote for PFF. "He tallied 81 and 83 pressures in 2024 and 2025, and is coming off a 2025 season that saw him earn a career-high 76.6 PFF grade. His 50 combined sacks and quarterback hits in the regular season and playoffs last year were the most in the league."

It would be nice to see Allen earn a little more recognition here, but he is going to be one of the leaders of the Broncos' defense and one of the most difficult players for opposing offenses to deal with.

#Broncos DL Zach Allen: “We came close to the sack record last year. And we fully expect to break it this year.” pic.twitter.com/652koOZTPO

In three seasons with the Broncos, Allen has notched 20.5 sacks while placing pressure on the quarterback on seemingly every passing play. Last year, he also knocked down six passes at the line of scrimmage, adding a new wrinkle to his game. He had never had more than one in a season before that.

Prepared to begin his fourth season in Denver, the Broncos are happy they have Allen, and the list of players they'd prefer over him would likely be rather short.

title: Raiders' Kirk Cousins blasts Maxx Crosby & Texans for rough NFL preseason physicality
description: Kirk Cousins had a stern reminder for the Raiders, Texans, and Maxx Crosby amid the physicality he faced during their NFL preseason matchups.
fullText:
Raiders' Kirk Cousins blasts Maxx Crosby & Texans for rough NFL preseason physicality originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

NFL Preseason is typically when the physicality ramps up. Defenses are more eager to simulate their full strength against receivers, tight ends, and quarterbacks. There are obviously upsides to this, but Kirk Cousins doesn't seem to appreciate it when some players go over the line a bit. In the past few weeks, he has called for certain players and teams to chill out a bit since the games do not count yet. The Las Vegas Raiders, Houston Texans, and even Maxx Crosby got blasted after the veteran quarterback had enough.

Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is around the corner. Plenty of teams are practicing the schemes they formulated in the offseason and starting to turn the dial up on execution. Kirk Cousins understands that, but he made a plea to a lot of squads he was facing. He asked them to calm down a bit when taking him down.

Cousins specifically asked Maxx Crosby, the rest of the Raiders defense, and the Texans not to be too harsh with his arm. The 14-year veteran wants to stay on the field for a long time, and all this roughness during the NFL Preseason does not seem to be helping, via Adam Hill of The Las Vegas Review-Journal.

"My elbow got hit. I joke with Maxx, and I say, 'You can touch me anywhere you want, just don't touch my arm.' You want to bump me in the ribs? Fine. I think if anything, hitting me in the hips or the ribs is actually good because it simulates what I need to feel. I've got some scars from some hits in real games where helmets go into armpits and things, and it ruins your season. So, I was just asking Crosby to just stay off the arm, and I had to remind the Texans as well," the Raiders quarterback declared.

Notably, Cousins sustained a shoulder injury back in the 2024 NFL season. Since then, his numbers haven't been the best. During his last two years with the Atlanta Falcons, he also got sacked 41 times. At one point, the quarterback even led the league with 16 interceptions back in 2024 because of how bad his arm situation was.

"I might as well just take the red jersey off because you're playing with, sometimes, an understood rule that if it's not understood, then what are we doing?" Cousins added.

The Raiders quarterback does have a point here. He did wear a jersey, which meant that the no-contact rule was in place during their NFL preseason joint practices and drills. Yet, Crosby, the Raiders defense, and the Texans were all still fairly rough in taking him down. It all came to a head when Crosby and Cousins had to be benched from team drills a few weeks back.

Hopefully, this plea to the Raiders and other defenses would help Cousins and the other quarterbacks during the NFL Preseason. It's one thing to have their season cut short during the 17-game campaign, but not getting to experience it all after a lengthy offseason is a different kind of bummer.

title: Spicy joint practice between Cowboys and Saints erupts into multiple brawls, ejection
description: The dog days of summer are in full effect, and NFL training camps are taking their toll.
fullText:
The dog days of summer are in full effect, and NFL training camps are taking their toll.

Take, for instance, Tuesday's joint practice between the Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints in Oxnard, California. The NFC rivals squared off for a full practice in pads. That meant competing, hitting and some guys performing for their jobs.

The result was a scrimmage that was spicy throughout and eventually erupted to multiple big fights and the ejection of Cowboys defensive end Donovan Ezeiruaku.

There was the normal pushing and shoving that should be expected from any sort of joint practice. This involved Saints wide receiver Chris Olave and Cowboys safety Malik Hooker, among others.

Chris Olave getting in Malik Hooker's face.

Brevyn Spann-Ford gets into it with a Saints player because that’s just how the day is going. pic.twitter.com/vplYblVwRt

But things really got heated multiple times as full-on fights broke out between pretty much all the players on the field.

BAH GAWD THAT'S BROCK RECHSTEINER'S MUSIC!#Saints and #Cowboys in another huge fight.

Wait for the slam at 0:17: pic.twitter.com/hDt71jfnbC

Things are getting way out of hand at Cowboys-Saints pic.twitter.com/6dz65OnRG9

He acknowledged that "it was chippy on both sides."

When asked who won the fights, Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson offered a less restrained response, per The Athletic's Jon Machota.

"Of course we did," Thompson said. "Come on, now."

Jerry Jones and the Dallas Cowboys enter the 2026 NFL season with hopes of getting back to the playoffs and being a Super Bowl contender.

Throughout the course of the offseason, the Cowboys were heavily rumored to make a big splash addition. That opportunity never ended up materializing for Dallas.

Among the most notable offseason moves were the trade for pass rusher Rashan Gary, trading up in the NFL Draft to get Caleb Downs, and the decision to franchise tag wide receiver George Pickens instead of giving him a contract extension. Despite the lack of a blockbuster move, the Cowboys feel that they have improved the roster.

In recent years, Dallas has continually come up short of expectations. Jones has been very vocal about being willing to do whatever it takes to get the Cowboys back to the Super Bowl.

With that being said, a former NFL star and Super Bowl winner has spoken out with a strong shot directed at the Dallas franchise owner.

Mark Schlereth, a Denver Broncos' legend, recently took a shot at Jones on social media. The shot came after a question from a fan.

"Mark! Do you think it's Jerry's ego or ignorance that is holding the cowboys back?" the fan questioned.

The response from Schlereth included just three words.

"All the above," Schlereth wrote.

Jones has always been one of the most polarizing team owners in professional sports. He is heavily involved in roster moves and franchise decisions. At times, the Cowboys could be better off without him involving himself in those choices.

As previously mentioned, Jones has been very vocal about his desire to be a championship contender. Should Dallas come up short of those expectations, changes could be made.

Throughout his tenure as the Cowboys' owner, Jones hasn't always been patient. He wants to win and coming up short of that can trigger a quick decision.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is entering his second season as the head coach in Dallas. He has received strong praise from Jones, but missing the playoffs in 2026 could bring a coaching change. The roster is also facing pressure, as Jones could get extremely aggressive and overhaul many positions with another disappointing year.

Only time will tell what Dallas is able to accomplish this season. For Jones, the time to win is now. His clock is ticking and he is expecting the Cowboys to take a big step forward from where they were a year ago.

title: LA Rams Sign Australian Punter Cut by 49ers Ahead of Melbourne Opener
description: The Los Angeles Rams have added an Australian specialist less than a month before opening the regular season in Melbourne against the team that recently let him go.KPRC 2 NFL insider Aaron Wilson reported on Aug. 16 that the Rams signed punter Jack Bouwmeester, a 27-year-old rookie who spent training camp with the San Francisco […] The post LA Rams Sign Australian Punter Cut by 49ers Ahead of Melbourne Opener appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams have added an Australian specialist less than a month before opening the regular season in Melbourne against the team that recently let him go.

KPRC 2 NFL insider Aaron Wilson reported on Aug. 16 that the Rams signed punter Jack Bouwmeester, a 27-year-old rookie who spent training camp with the San Francisco 49ers before being waived four days earlier.

Los Angeles will face San Francisco on Sept. 10 in the United States — Sept. 11 locally — at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia.

Bouwmeester grew up in Australia before beginning a lengthy college career in the United States.

As for Los Angeles, the addition arrives one day after incumbent punter Ethan Evans delivered a productive showing in the team's 20-12 preseason victory over the Kansas City Chiefs.

Evans punted four times for 243 yards, averaging 60.8 yards with a long of 65 and two kicks landing inside the 20-yard line.

Bouwmeester's first NFL stop lasted less than a month.

The 49ers officially signed him to a three-year contract on July 18 after he went undrafted out of Texas. He entered camp competing with veteran Corliss Waitman for San Francisco's punting job, with the organization describing the competition as open during the first week of August.

That battle ended sooner than expected.

San Francisco waived Bouwmeester on Aug. 12 while signing cornerback Eli Apple, defensive lineman Xavier Thomas and running back Zamir White. Waitman remained as the lone punter on the roster.

Bouwmeester has enjoyed extensive college action despite entering the NFL as a rookie. He appeared in 53 games across stops at Michigan State, Utah and Texas, recording 213 punts for 9,338 yards and a 43.8-yard average, according to the 49ers.

He averaged 44.5 yards on 59 punts during his final season at Texas.

Before that, Bouwmeester averaged 44.7 yards at Utah in 2024 and earned second-team All-Big 12 recognition. He was a first-team All-Pac-12 selection in 2023 after averaging 45.5 yards per punt and placing 20 attempts inside the 20-yard line.

Bouwmeester's arrival doesn't suggest Evans' job is in serious jeopardy.

Evans entered his fourth season with Los Angeles after spending the offseason adjusting his mechanics.

He told the Rams' official website that shortening his steps helped improve his hang time and consistency, and new special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone praised the progress Evans showed during the offseason.

His performance against Kansas City brought forth mrore evidence that those adjustments are seeing daylight in preseason action.

Nonetheless, the Rams now have another option in Bouwmeester as teams work through roster evaluations before the regular season.

In the end, how likely is it that the same Australian punter who spent the summer trying to earn the San Francisco's job travels home with Los Angeles instead to face his former team at the MCG?

His addition clearly comes with a unique storyline waiting in Week 1.
